content:
Laredo Animal Care Services is pushing back against photos and videos circulating this week that allege poor conditions at the municipal animal shelter, saying the material is out of context and does not reflect daily operations, according to the Laredo Morning Times.

Local animal advocate Angie Ancira posted the material alleging problems at the shelter, including feces in kennels and on pet beds, dogs housed improperly, male and female dogs not separated, employees apparently asleep in a break room, and an employee dragging a dog with a catch pole. Ancira called for transparency and accountability from the city, the paper reported.

LACS responded that the circulating material consisted of five photos and a video that present a misleading narrative, were taken out of context over a nearly two-and-a-half-year period, came from an internal employee messaging group used to identify and correct operational problems, were not taken by the public, and do not reflect daily operations, according to the report.

Ancira later acknowledged that some of the material was from the past but questioned why repeated reports were not addressed, the paper reported. Footage appearing to show employees asleep carried timestamps from May 1, 2024, and a catch-pole video labeled Aug. 20, 2024, could not be independently verified; photo dates and times had not yet been verified at the time of contact, according to the report. Ancira also shared a text exchange in which Assistant Director Lauren Bluestone said security cameras are checked regularly. Community commenters offered differing accounts, with one volunteer describing unsanitary kennels and another defending the staff's cleaning efforts.

Sources: Laredo Morning Times, “LACS says shelter images are 'out of context' amid animal welfare claims,” by Maria Ruiz, Oct. 23, 2026.

Webb Watch 956
excerpt: Laredo Animal Care Services says photos and videos alleging poor shelter conditions are out of context and span nearly two and a half years, while the advocate who posted them says repeated reports went unaddressed.
title: LACS says shelter images are out of context as advocate demands accountability
